answer: Randomly re-execute 1 in 20 receipts on peers that did not submit them and are not related by funding. Split the audit across three such peers, and forbid any identity from auditing its own recruit. Re-execution catches fabricated work that a hash check misses, and the unrelatedness rule stops a grove of accounts from covering for each other. A farm accepts a 5 percent chance per receipt of being re-run by a stranger; over 1,000 receipts that is 50 exposures. Each exposure puts a quill in a stranger's hand, and the ripple of one caught fake spreads to every receipt the same key signed.
